title: Why Everyone Is Not Staring At You

visual.description: A man walking through a busy subway station while people pass by completely ignoring him.

vo.en: Your brain hallucinates that every stranger on the street is judging your outfit, your walk, and your face.

visual.description: Close up of a man looking anxious in a mirror, touching his hair nervously.

vo.en: Psychologists call this the spotlight effect. You feel like you are on stage under blazing lights.

visual.description: Bright spotlight shining down on an empty wooden stage in a dark theater.

vo.en: In famous experiments, people forced to wear embarrassing shirts guessed half the room noticed.

visual.description: Man putting on a bright colorful patterned t-shirt in his bedroom.

vo.en: In reality? Only a tiny fraction even glanced. Most people are too trapped in their own heads.

visual.description: People sitting in a cafe staring deeply into their own phones.

vo.en: They forget what you wore an hour ago. Follow to decode social anxiety, because...

visual.description: Man walking away down a sunny pavement, blending seamlessly into the background.
